parts.note: to check something is to test it
a flight is a set of steps or stairs

explanation.surface: A nervous passenger is told to check the boarding steps before an airliner's first trip.
explanation.walkthrough: The 9 is a cross-reference to 9-down, AIRLINER: the first trip of a new jet is its trial run.
explanation.definitionFit: A new aircraft's maiden journey is a trial run in the air to prove it works.

clue.text: Grave in honour of the doctor

parts.note: a toast or dedication is made 'to' someone, in their honour
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A grave is dug in memory of the late family physician.
explanation.definitionFit: A burial vault or monument where a body lies is a synonym for a grave.

clue.text: Table piece, no less valuable for having lumps in it

definitions.text: Table piece, no less valuable for having lumps in it

parts.words: Table piece, no less valuable for having lumps in it
parts.note: a piece of tableware whose worth is not reduced by being lumpy, because it is meant to hold lumps of something sweet

explanation.surface: A piece of furniture or china is still prized despite its bumps and dents.
explanation.definitionFit: This tea-table vessel exists to hold sweetener cubes, so lumps inside are its whole purpose.

clue.text: Fellow with operations gives all the details

parts.note: F is an abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS
acts are deeds or operations carried out

explanation.surface: A colleague who handles operations supplies the full particulars.
explanation.definitionFit: The full particulars of a matter are its known truths, the information.

definitions.meaning: written as poetry, in lines of verse
turned the other way up, reversed in position

explanation.definitionFit: Poetry is composed in metrical lines, and a mathematical or positional reversal is an opposite or inverted thing.

indicators.note: the negative and earth pieces go inside the name of the king

parts.note: Henry is the name of eight English kings
N is the abbreviation for negative, as on a battery terminal
E is the abbreviation for earth in electrical wiring

explanation.surface: An electrician wires the negative and earth terminals of a big royal battery.
explanation.walkthrough: The electrical words make 'battery' look like a power cell; it is a battery of hens, which is what a hen-house holds.
explanation.definitionFit: A poultry farm or hen-house is where laying hens are kept, as in a battery farm.

clue.text: The last we see of Coney, say?

definitions.text: The last we see of Coney, say?

parts.words: The last we see of Coney, say?
parts.note: a coney is an old word for a rabbit, and the last part of it seen as it bolts away is its short white tail

explanation.surface: A traveller takes a final look back at Coney Island.
explanation.definitionFit: A rabbit's or hare's short tail is the white flash seen as the animal runs off.

definitions.meaning: to fasten firmly or grip tight
a wheel lock fitted to an illegally parked car

explanation.definitionFit: To fasten something tightly is to grip it in a vice, and a wheel lock immobilising a car is a device of that name.

clue.text: Walker risking prosecution, according to the signs

definitions.text: Walker risking prosecution, according to the signs

parts.words: Walker risking prosecution, according to the signs
parts.note: warning notices on private land say that anyone wandering on to it without permission will be prosecuted

explanation.surface: A hiker is warned by notices that legal action may follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Signs reading 'will be prosecuted' address the intruder who walks on private land without leave.

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece sits over, that is above, the other

parts.note: air is wind or moving breath
a liner is a protective sleeve, as for a record

explanation.surface: Wind blows over someone's sleeve.
explanation.definitionFit: A passenger jet aircraft operated by an airline is a large commercial plane.

clue.text: Free from blame, a number point out

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five, a number
to indicate is to point out

explanation.surface: Someone cleared of blame points out a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear someone's name is to justify or exonerate them.

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the word Penny's

parts.note: to husband resources is to save or reserve them

explanation.surface: Penny holds on to her first husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'husband' looks like a noun after 'first'; it is the verb meaning to conserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something is to conserve it or maintain it unchanged.

parts.note: LA, Los Angeles, is a city
a pup is a cheeky young person, a whippersnapper

explanation.surface: A city youngster takes pleasure in things.
explanation.definitionFit: To relish something eagerly is to drink it in like a cat with milk.

clue.text: Simple diet prepared for seventy on the way

indicators.note: a diet that is prepared is made up, so its letters are made up afresh

explanation.surface: A plain eating plan is got ready for a seventy-year-old travelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seventy' looks like an age; it is 70 mph, the maximum on British motorways.
explanation.definitionFit: The maximum legal road speed, 70 mph on UK motorways, is the cap on how fast you may drive.

definitions.meaning: to put forward a plan or idea
to nominate someone for a post

explanation.definitionFit: Putting forward a suggestion and nominating a candidate are both to put something up for consideration.

clue.text: Neat spirits to be kept up for this bird

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox
'keep your pecker up' is a British idiom meaning keep your spirits up, so pecker means spirits

explanation.surface: Neat spirits are kept on a high shelf for the birdwatcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Neat spirits' reads as undiluted drink; neat is cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: The oxpecker is an African bird that feeds on ticks on the backs of cattle and other grazing animals.

indicators.note: putting the words in order means rearranging their letters

explanation.surface: Troops from the north look for anyone to give them orders.
explanation.definitionFit: In the American Civil War the Union troops of the North were nicknamed after New Englanders.

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word save is read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: IV is four in Roman numerals
Ely is a cathedral city, a bishop's see

explanation.surface: Someone slyly saves up four, understand?
explanation.definitionFit: Acting cunningly means dodging directly answering, in an elusive way.

parts.note: reads as a tan on the torso, but the upper body is a heavenly body such as the sun or moon being obscured

explanation.surface: A sunbather's chest goes darker.
explanation.definitionFit: When the moon passes before the sun, a celestial body is obscured and goes dark.

parts.note: reads as a drought or empty tank, but it is the time when the sea goes back from the shore

explanation.surface: A household or town finds its water supply exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: The receding of the sea after high water is the falling tide.

clue.text: Battery of gunners in flat boat

indicators.note: the gunners are placed inside the word for the flat boat

parts.note: a barge is a flat-bottomed boat
RA, the Royal Artillery, are gunners

explanation.surface: A battery of artillerymen is carried on a flat-bottomed vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A battery is a heavy concentrated bombardment of guns, a sustained artillery onslaught.

clue.text: … he goes in, as a striker

definitions.text: … he goes in, as a striker

parts.words: … he goes in, as a striker
parts.note: continues from the previous clue's barrage: a player who goes in to bat in cricket and strikes the ball

explanation.surface: After the bombardment, a man goes in on the attack.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket each side's players go in, one after another, to hit the ball; the striker is the one facing the bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the player at the crease who hits the ball is called the striker.

indicators.note: wild suggests the letters run free in a new order

explanation.surface: I call out wildly about a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale purple colour named after a flowering shrub is a shade.

clue.text: Road connections for St Andrews, for example

definitions.meaning: St Andrews in Scotland is the most famous seaside golf course

explanation.definitionFit: Connections are ties or joins, and a seaside golf course on sandy ground is also called by this name.

parts.note: to bathe is to go for a swim

indicators.note: brought back means the word it is turned round to run the other way

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on a tap

explanation.surface: A swim brought back a chill and a sense of anticlimax.
explanation.definitionFit: Bathos is a ludicrous drop from the sublime to the trivial, so this adjective means letdown.

indicators.note: letters made to differ from their order are rearranged

explanation.surface: Worried? Let's agree to disagree.
explanation.definitionFit: Keen and impatient to do something, as in anxious to please.

parts.note: a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, and an egg is a zero shape, so nil

explanation.surface: A pale duck-egg blue colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck-egg blue' is a real paint shade, so the eye reads it as one; the definition is just 'blue'.
explanation.definitionFit: Anil is the indigo plant and the deep blue dye made from it.

definitions.meaning: a habitual personal gesture or quirk
a sixteenth-century European art style that followed the High Renaissance

explanation.definitionFit: A habitual quirk of behaviour and the late Renaissance artistic style share the same name.

definitions.meaning: read as common place, a village common where people gather

explanation.definitionFit: The shade of grass, and a public grassy area in a village, the common place.

clue.text: Sets out to be a hardy girl, we are told

indicators.note: out signals the letters are thrown out of their order

explanation.surface: A girl tough enough to set out on her own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hardy' looks like an adjective meaning tough; it is Thomas Hardy, whose novel heroine is of the d'Urbervilles.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Hardy's novel tells of a doomed heroine of the d'Urbervilles, a girl of that name.

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for penny
royal means princely, fit for a prince

explanation.surface: A stammering speaker calls a plant princely.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammer 'P-princely' gives a separate P before 'princely'.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-growing mint whose oil was once used medicinally is a herb of this name.
